classification.difficultyReason: A supplied cooling model is verified and used through scaffolded substitution, logarithms, limiting behaviour and graphing.

content.prompt: A cup full of coffee initially has temperature $70^\circ\mathrm{C}$, and it sits in a room of temperature $20^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The temperature of the coffee cup can be modelled by the differential equation $$\frac{dT}{dt}=k(T-B),$$ where $B$ is the temperature of the room and $T$ is the temperature of the coffee cup after $t$ minutes.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $T=20+50e^{kt}$ satisfies the differential equation.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}T&=20+50e^{kt}\\\frac{dT}{dt}&=50ke^{kt}\\&=k(50e^{kt})\\&=k(20+50e^{kt}-20)\\&=k(T-20)\\&=k(T-B).\end{align*}$$ Thus the differential equation is satisfied, since $B=20$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: After ten minutes, the temperature of the coffee cup reduces to $50^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Find the value of $k$ in exact form.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the temperature of the coffee cup after five minutes? Give your answer to the nearest degree Celsius.

children.label: d
children.prompt: After how many minutes, to the nearest minute, will the temperature drop below $30^\circ\mathrm{C}$?

answer.worked: Find the time at which the temperature reaches $30^\circ\mathrm{C}$: $$\begin{align*}30&=20+50e^{kt}\\10&=50e^{kt}\\e^{kt}&=\frac15\\kt&=\ln\left(\frac15\right)\\t&=\frac{\ln(1/5)}{k}\\&=\frac{10\ln(1/5)}{\ln(3/5)}\\&\approx31.51\text{ minutes}.\end{align*}$$ Since the temperature is decreasing, it is below $30^\circ\mathrm{C}$ after this time, or approximately $32$ minutes to the nearest minute.

children.label: e
children.prompt: What is the limiting temperature of the coffee?

children.label: f
children.prompt: Draw a graph of the temperature against time, labelling all important features.

answer.short: A decreasing, concave-up exponential curve for $t\ge0$, starting at $(0,70)$ and approaching the horizontal asymptote $T=20$ from above.
answer.worked: $T(0)=70$. Since $k<0$, $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=50ke^{kt}<0$ and $\dfrac{d^2T}{dt^2}=50k^2e^{kt}>0$. The curve decreases from $70^\circ\mathrm{C}$, is concave up and approaches $T=20$ as $t\to\infty$.

spec.sourceRegion: Part f supplied answer graph, lower left
spec.description: Axes extend slightly into negative directions. The temperature axis has labels 70 and 20; the time axis has no numeric ticks. A blue decreasing, concave-up curve starts at T=70 and approaches a dashed blue T=20 asymptote, with an arrow at the curve's right end.
spec.mathematics: T(t)=20+50exp(ln(3/5)t/10), t>=0; initial value 70; horizontal asymptote T=20.
